text.p: Shares in Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc opened 3.8 percent higher at 6.70 francs in Paris after the company said it would have no financial impact from the recent fire.
The share has fallen in an almost unbroken line from 7.80 francs on November 18, the day of the fire, to a close of 6.45 francs on Tuesday.

"We are under no financial pressure because we have insurance which covers our operating losses," co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle told Europe 1 radio. He said the loss of earnings could be "significant" but give no figure.
Ponsolle said Eurotunnel hopes the Eurostar high-speed train service between Britain and France can resume service at the start of next week.
Full repairs in the fire-damaged tunnel could take three to five months to complete, he added.
At 0909 GMT, Eurotunnel was up 3.1 percent at 6.65 francs after having hit a day-high of 6.85 francs.
